results.title: TK — A new way to write from Medium | Tony Stubblebine | 13 comments
results.content:
Here we go. Big thing from Medium! We want to be your daily writing app... ideas, notes, drafts, research, deep thinking. To that end, meet TK, an agentic notebook for writing and thinking.  The why now is that we are betting on human intelligence. The why now is that we are betting on human intelligence. Much of the AI industry is betting that machines will do our thinking for us, and some of its leaders talk as if writing no longer matters. We’re betting the other way. We’re not anti-AI, we’re pro-human. The agentic era runs on words. The logic of this era is that if you capture your intelligence through words, the agentic era will amplify them. It's just a really, really good time to be someone who likes to write. So that's our design POV: encourage you to write more, gather your ideas [...] Tony, I've given up on Medium again, and I've lost count of how many times I've walked away. I've been writing for 50 years, and at 70, I deal with memory issues that make writing more challenging. AI has helped me continue doing something I love. It helps me organize my thoughts, develop ideas, and express myself while preserving the voice I've cultivated over a lifetime. My frustration is that AI-assisted writing seems to be treated as inferior, even when the ideas, direction, judgment, and voice are entirely human. Meanwhile, plenty of shallow, repetitive, poorly written human content proliferates on Medium. Human-written slop is still slop. You say the agentic era will amplify human intelligence. That's precisely how I use AI. Yet my experience suggests Medium discourages this [...] Zack R.   13h

It’s encouraging to see this come to fruition whilst I’ve concurrently been building my own prose platform around a related premise—with no AI in the writing surface, deliberately. For my own practice, that constraint is a feature. Human-authored. Human-directed. Machine-readable. The overlap is treating writing as a place to develop thinking, not just produce content. results.title: Medium Opens TK Notebook to Writers with Inline AI Assistance – Unite.AI
results.content:
## AI Assistance Inside the Draft

Writers can type @TK in the middle of a sentence to check a fact or retrieve earlier writing without leaving the editor. The name adapts the publishing placeholder TK, meaning “to come,” which writers traditionally leave for unfinished information. Here, the placeholder can trigger the assistant instead, keeping research and retrieval from interrupting the draft.

AI feedback covers editorial and headline suggestions, can compare drafts with Medium publications’ style guides, and can flag material that could be organized into a book. Medium says TK will not write a user’s essay, positioning the assistant as support for the writer’s own work rather than a substitute for it. [...] The wider opening follows Medium’s September 16, 2026 post, which described TK as invite-only or available to Friends of Medium while broader access was being prepared. TK is separate from Medium’s publishing platform; chief executive Tony Stubblebine’s shorthand for the division is “TK is the gym and Medium is the stage.”

The first version includes a mobile app and widgets for voice and text capture, imports of Medium archives and Bear or Obsidian vaults, and Markdown import and export. It ships without a native desktop app, which Stubblebine said Medium wants to add.

## AI Assistance Inside the Draft [...] ## Agents, Sharing and Provenance

Beyond its built-in assistant, TK includes an MCP server and Claude skill so agents can draw on a user’s stored positions, projects and unfinished ideas. Medium’s Claude Daily Note plugin shows how that connection works: with TK’s MCP server connected in Claude Cowork or Claude Code, the plugin creates one document per day, updates it in place and carries unchecked to-do items forward. Its targeted edit operations are designed to preserve live edits, existing checkbox states and the user’s writing.
